p.src: That night, she and Ping'er sat by the brazier beneath the lamplight, wearily plying their needles. Having already ordered the embroidered quilts to be richly perfumed, they lay down and counted on their fingers how far the travelers should have gone; before they knew it, the third watch had begun. Ping'er was already fast asleep. Just as Xifeng's bright eyes began to grow heavy, she dimly saw Madam Qin enter from outside and say with a smile, “Aunt, how soundly you sleep! I am leaving today, yet you will not even see me on my way. We have always been close, and I could not bear to part from you, so I came to bid you farewell. There is also one wish of mine still unfulfilled. I must tell you of it, for no one else may prove equal to the task.”

p.src: Hearing this, Xifeng asked hazily, “What wish is that? Entrust it to me without hesitation.” Madam Qin said, “Aunt, you are a heroine among women; even those men in caps and girdles cannot surpass you. How can you fail to understand two common sayings? It is often said, ‘When the moon is full, it begins to wane; when water brims, it overflows.’ And again, ‘The higher the climb, the harder the fall.’ Our house has now enjoyed dazzling glory for nearly a hundred years. If one day joy should give birth to sorrow, and the saying ‘When the tree falls, the monkeys scatter’ should come true, would we not have claimed in vain to be an ancient family of learning and refinement? These words greatly stirred Xifeng's mind and filled her with reverence. She hurriedly asked, “Your concern is entirely justified, but is there any means by which we may remain forever secure?” Madam Qin gave a cold laugh. “How foolish you are, Aunt. Misfortune reaches its limit and yields to fortune; honor and disgrace have alternated in endless cycles since ancient times. How could human effort preserve prosperity forever? But if, while still prosperous, we can lay the foundations that will sustain the family in future decline, that may indeed be called lasting preservation. At present almost everything is properly arranged, but two matters remain unsettled. If they are dealt with as I propose, the family's future security may be assured.”

p.src: Xifeng asked what those matters were. Madam Qin replied, “Although sacrifices are now offered at the ancestral graves in all four seasons, no fixed funds or grain have been assigned to them. Secondly, though the family school has been established, it has no secure endowment. As I see it, while the family flourishes there will naturally be no lack of funds for sacrifices and maintenance. But when decline comes, from what source will these two expenses be met? It would be best to follow my settled plan: while the family is wealthy and honored, purchase more farms, houses, and fields near the ancestral graves, so that all expenses for sacrifices and maintenance may be drawn from them, and establish the family school there as well. Gather the elders and juniors of the clan to establish regulations, and thereafter let each branch in turn administer for one year the land, revenues, sacrifices, and provisions. With management rotating in this way, there will be no rivalry, nor such abuses as mortgaging or selling the property. Even if the family should be convicted of a crime and all other property confiscated, not even the authorities may seize an estate dedicated to ancestral sacrifices. Even if the house falls into ruin, its descendants may return home to study and farm, and still have somewhere to retreat, while the ancestral sacrifices can continue forever. If we now suppose that our splendor will never end and give no thought to the future, it will prove no lasting policy. Within a few days, another extraordinary cause for rejoicing will arise before our eyes, adding oil to the blazing fire and brocade to a mass of flowers. Yet you must understand that this too will be no more than a moment's magnificence and a brief spell of joy. Never forget the saying, ‘Even the grandest feast must end.’ Unless plans for the future are made early, I fear that when the time comes, regret will be of no avail.” Xifeng hurriedly asked, “What happy event is this?” Madam Qin answered, “The secrets of Heaven must not be divulged. But since you and I have been close, I shall give you two lines at our parting. You must remember them.” She then recited:

p.src: To leave idle matters aside, Baoyu had been forlorn since Lin Daiyu's recent departure. He no longer played with anyone and went listlessly to bed every evening. Now, hearing in his sleep that Lady Qin had died, he hastily rolled over and scrambled up. He felt such unbearable pain, as though a knife had pierced his heart, that with a cry he suddenly coughed up a mouthful of blood. Xiren and the others rushed forward in alarm to support him, asking what was wrong, and were about to inform Grandmother Jia and summon a physician. Baoyu said with a smile, “There is no need to fuss. It is nothing serious—sudden grief has attacked my heart and driven the blood from its proper channels.” As he spoke, he rose and called for clothes so that he could change, see Grandmother Jia, and go over there at once. Seeing him in this state, Xiren could not set her mind at ease, yet dared not restrain him and could only let him have his way. When Grandmother Jia saw that he meant to go, she said, “A place where someone has only just breathed her last is unclean. Besides, the wind is strong at night. It will not be too late to go tomorrow morning.” But Baoyu would not consent. Grandmother Jia ordered a carriage prepared and sent a large retinue of attendants to escort him there. When they reached the Ningguo Mansion, its gates stood wide open, and lanterns on either side made the scene as bright as day. People came and went in noisy confusion, while the wailing within seemed to shake the mountains. Baoyu alighted from the carriage and hurried to the chamber where the coffin rested, there weeping bitterly for some time. Afterward, he went to pay his respects to Lady You. As it happened, Lady You's old stomach ailment had returned, and she lay confined to bed. He then came out again to see Jia Zhen. By then Jia Dairu, Daixiu, Jia Chi, Jia Xiao, Jia Dun, Jia She, Jia Zheng, Jia Cong, Jia Ban, Jia Heng, Jia Guang, Jia Chen, Jia Qiong, Jia Lin, Jia Qiang, Jia Chang, Jia Ling, Jia Yun, Jia Qin, Jia Zhen, Jia Ping, Jia Zao, Jia Heng, Jia Fen, Jia Fang, Jia Lan, Jia Jun, Jia Zhi, and the rest had all arrived. Jia Zhen, his face drenched with tears, was saying to Jia Dairu and the others, “Everyone in the household and all our relatives and friends, near and far, knows that this daughter-in-law of mine was ten times better than a son. Now that she has stretched out her legs and gone, it is clear that there is no one left to carry on the senior branch.” With that, he began weeping again. The others hastened to console him: “She has already departed this life, and weeping will do no good. What matters now is to discuss how the funeral should be arranged.” Jia Zhen clapped his hands and cried, “How shall it be arranged? I shall simply devote everything I possess to it!” As he spoke, Qin Ye and Qin Zhong arrived, together with several of Lady You's relatives and her sisters. Jia Zhen ordered Jia Qiong, Jia Chen, Jia Lin, and Jia Qiang to entertain the guests. At the same time, he sent for the astrologers of the Imperial Observatory to choose an auspicious date. They settled upon keeping the coffin for seven sevens, forty-nine days, and opening the formal mourning and sending out obituary notices three days later.

p.src: Throughout those forty-nine days, one hundred and eight Buddhist monks were engaged to perform the Great Compassion Repentance in the main hall, delivering the souls of all who had died before or since and absolving the deceased of sin. A separate altar was erected in the Tianxiang Tower, where ninety-nine Quanzhen Taoist priests conducted rites for forty-nine days to release grievances and cleanse karmic transgressions. The coffin was then placed in Huifang Garden. Before it, another fifty eminent Buddhist monks and fifty eminent Taoist priests faced one another at separate altars and performed services at each of the seven weekly observances. When Jia Jing learned that his eldest grandson's wife had died, he reflected that he himself would attain immortality sooner or later. How could he consent to return home, become tainted once more by the mortal world, and throw away all his previous spiritual efforts? He therefore paid the matter no heed and left Jia Zhen to arrange everything.

p.src: Seeing that his father took no part, Jia Zhen gave free rein to extravagance. When coffin boards were inspected, several sets of fir planks were all found unsuitable. As luck would have it, Xue Pan came to offer his condolences. Seeing Jia Zhen searching for fine boards, he said, “Our timber shop has a set of planks from some wood called qiang, which grows on Iron Net Mountain by the Huang Sea. Made into a coffin, it will last ten thousand years without decay. My late father brought it back years ago. It was originally intended for the venerable Prince Yizhong, but after he fell into disgrace, it was never collected. It remains sealed up in the shop, and no one has dared even to name a price for it. If you want it, simply have it carried here and use it.” Jia Zhen was overjoyed to hear this and immediately ordered men to bring it. When everyone examined the planks, they saw that the sides and bottom were each eight inches thick. Their grain resembled betel nut, their fragrance sandalwood and musk, and when struck by hand, they rang like gold and jade. Everyone marveled at it and sang its praises. Jia Zhen asked with a smile, “What is it worth?” Xue Pan laughed. “Even with a thousand taels of silver in hand, I fear you would find nowhere to buy its like. There is no question of a price. Just give the workmen a few taels for their labor.” On hearing this, Jia Zhen thanked him profusely and at once ordered the planks sawn apart, joined, and lacquered. Jia Zheng tried to dissuade him: “I fear this is not an object an ordinary person is entitled to use. Fine fir would suffice for the encoffinment.” But Jia Zhen now wished he could have died in Lady Qin's place, so how could he heed such advice? Then news suddenly came that one of Lady Qin's maids, Ruizhu, had dashed her head against a pillar and died upon seeing her mistress dead. This was a remarkable occurrence, and the entire clan exclaimed over it. Jia Zhen therefore had her encoffined and buried with the rites due a granddaughter, and her coffin was also placed in the Dengxian Pavilion in Huifang Garden. Another young maid named Baozhu, seeing that Lady Qin had left no children, willingly offered to become her adopted daughter and vowed to assume the duties of chief mourner and escort the bier. Jia Zhen was delighted beyond measure and immediately issued orders that Baozhu was henceforth to be addressed as Young Mistress. Observing the mourning rites of an unmarried daughter, Baozhu grieved before the coffin as though her heart would break. Thus every member of the clan and all the household servants carried out their respective duties according to the old conventions, and naturally no disorder was permitted.

p.src: Jia Zhen reflected that Jia Rong was no more than a student of the Imperial Academy; his title would look unimpressive when inscribed upon the spirit banners and sutra tablets, and there would be few ceremonial insignia to display. This left him deeply dissatisfied. As it happened, this was the fourth day of the first seven-day mourning period. Dai Quan, Chief Palace Eunuch of the Daming Palace, had already sent men ahead with sacrificial offerings; afterward he came in person to pay his respects, borne in a great sedan chair beneath a parasol, with gongs sounding before him. Jia Zhen hurried out to receive him, conducted him to the Doufeng Pavilion, and offered him tea. Having already formed a plan, Jia Zhen seized the opportunity to mention that he wished to purchase an official appointment for Jia Rong. Dai Quan understood his meaning and said with a smile, “I suppose you want to lend greater splendor to the funeral.” Jia Zhen hastily replied with a smile, “Your Excellency has understood me perfectly.” Dai Quan said, “As it happens, there is an excellent vacancy. Two posts are presently open among the three hundred Imperial Guards. Yesterday the third brother of the Marquis of Xiangyang came to ask a favor of me and brought fifteen hundred taels of silver, which is now at my house. You know that we have long been friends; whatever the circumstances, for his grandfather’s sake I agreed to it after a fashion. That leaves one vacancy. Fatty Feng, the Military Commissioner of Yongxing, also came asking to purchase it for his son, but I had no time to oblige him. Since it is our own boy who wants the appointment, have his particulars written out at once.” On hearing this, Jia Zhen immediately ordered, “Tell the men in the study to prepare the young master’s particulars properly and bring them here at once.” The page dared not delay. p.src: After reading it, Dai Quan passed it over his shoulder to a personal page to keep and said, “When you return, take this to Old Zhao, the senior official at the Ministry of Revenue. Give him my compliments and tell him to issue a warrant for a fifth-rank Imperial Guard post and provide a certificate as well. Have these particulars entered upon it. Tomorrow I shall come to collect the silver and send it over.” The page acknowledged the order, and Dai Quan took his leave. Jia Zhen pressed him earnestly to stay, but could not prevail and had no choice but to escort him to the mansion gate. Just as Dai Quan was about to enter his sedan chair, Jia Zhen asked, “Should I take the silver to the Ministry to settle the payment, or send it all together to Your Excellency’s residence?” Dai Quan replied, “If you go to the Ministry, you will only be made to pay more. It would be better to settle it at twelve hundred taels and simply send the silver to my house.” Jia Zhen thanked him profusely, saying, “When the mourning period is over, I shall personally bring my unworthy son to your residence to kowtow in gratitude.” With that, they parted.

p.src: Presently another herald’s cry was heard: the newcomer was the wife of Shi Ding, Marquis of Zhongjing. Lady Wang, Lady Xing, Xifeng, and the others had scarcely welcomed her into the principal apartments when the sacrificial offerings from the households of the Marquis of Jinxiang, the Marquis of Chuanning, and the Earl of Shoushan were seen arranged before the spirit altar. Soon afterward, the three noblemen alighted from their sedan chairs, and Jia Zheng and the others hurried forward to receive them and conduct them into the great hall. Friends and relations came and went in such numbers that they could not possibly be counted. Throughout those forty-nine days, the street outside the Ningguo Mansion stretched white with a ceaseless stream of mourners, while brilliantly arrayed officials came and went in throngs.

p.src: Jia Zhen ordered Jia Rong to change into auspicious official dress the next day and return after collecting his certificate of appointment. All the ceremonial insignia and other articles displayed before the spirit were thereafter provided according to the regulations for a fifth-rank official. The spirit tablet and memorial notices all bore the inscription: “Spirit Seat of the Honorable Lady Qin of the Jia Family, Graciously Invested by the Celestial Court.” The street-facing gates of the Garden of Gathered Fragrance were flung wide open, and music pavilions were hastily erected on either side. Two companies of blue-robed musicians performed at appointed hours, while pairs of ceremonial insignia stood in ranks, their swords, execution blades, and axes all perfectly aligned. Outside the gate stood a pair of vermilion boards facing each other, emblazoned with large gilded characters: “Imperial Guard in Attendance upon the Throne, Guardian of the Inner Court and the Forbidden Precincts.” Across the way a lofty proclamation platform had been raised, upon which Buddhist and Taoist clerics displayed matching proclamations. Written in large characters upon them were the words: “Funeral of the Honorable Lady Qin of the Jia Family, wife of the eldest grandson in the direct line of the hereditary Duke of Ningguo, and wife of the Imperial Guard in Attendance upon the Throne and Guardian of the Inner Court. In this central land amid the Four Great Continents, in this realm of peace that receives its mandate from Heaven, Wanxu, presiding officer of the Buddhist Registry and supreme director of the doctrine of Emptiness and Tranquillity, together with Yesheng, presiding officer of the Taoist Registry and supreme director of the doctrine of the Primordial Three-in-One, reverently perform the rites of purification, paying homage to Heaven and bowing before the Buddha”; there were also such phrases as, “We respectfully summon the guardian deities of the monasteries, the messengers, the merit recorders, and the other gods; may sacred grace be bestowed upon all and divine power guard the distant regions; a forty-nine-day rite upon land and water for the dispelling of calamity, the cleansing of sin, and the securing of peace.” There is no need to record all these tedious details.

p.src: Although Jia Zhen’s wishes were now fulfilled, Lady You’s old illness had flared up again in the inner apartments, leaving her unable to manage affairs. He feared that when titled ladies came and went, some breach of courtesy might occur and expose the family to ridicule, and so he remained uneasy. As he stood there worrying, Baoyu, who was beside him, asked, “Everything seems to have been properly arranged. What are you still worrying about, Cousin Zhen?” When Jia Zhen heard the question, he explained that there was no one in the inner apartments capable of taking charge. Baoyu listened and said with a smile, “What is difficult about that? I can recommend someone to take temporary charge for this month, and I guarantee everything will be handled properly.” Jia Zhen hurriedly asked, “Who is it?” Seeing that many friends and relatives were still seated nearby, Baoyu thought it improper to speak openly. He went to Jia Zhen’s side and whispered a few words in his ear. Jia Zhen was overjoyed when he heard the suggestion. Springing to his feet, he said with a smile, “That would indeed settle everything. Let us go at once.” As he spoke, he took Baoyu by the hand, bade farewell to the company, and headed toward the principal apartments.

p.src: As it happened, this was not one of the principal days of mourning, so few relatives and friends had come. Inside, only a few close female relatives were present: Lady Xing, Lady Wang, Xifeng, and the women of the clan sat together keeping company. Then someone announced, “The master is coming in.” The old serving women scattered in alarm and scrambled to hide in the rear; Xifeng alone rose unhurriedly. Jia Zhen himself was somewhat unwell, and his excessive grief had weakened him further, so he hobbled in leaning on a crutch. Lady Xing and the others said, “You are unwell, and you have had so much to attend to these past few days. You ought to rest. What have you come in here for?” Supporting himself on his crutch, Jia Zhen struggled to bend his knees and kneel, meaning to pay his respects and apologize for troubling them. Lady Xing and the others hurriedly told Baoyu to support him and ordered a chair brought for him. Jia Zhen absolutely refused to sit. Forcing a smile, he said, “I have come in because there is something I must ask of my two aunts and my dear cousin.” Lady Xing and the others promptly asked, “What is it?” Jia Zhen hastened to say with a smile, “Aunt, you naturally know that now my grandson’s wife is gone, while my own wife has fallen ill. The inner household is truly in a disgraceful state. If my dear cousin would condescend to spend a month here and put things in order, I could set my mind at ease.” Lady Xing laughed. “So that is what this is about. Your cousin now belongs to your second aunt’s household, so you need only ask your second aunt.” Lady Wang hurriedly said, “She is still only a young girl and has never dealt with anything like this. If she fails to manage it properly, people will only laugh at her. You had better trouble someone else.” Jia Zhen smiled. “I understand what you mean, Aunt. You are afraid the work will be too hard on my cousin. But as for her being unable to manage, I guarantee that she can. Even if she makes a minor mistake, others will still see nothing amiss. Even as a child, when she was only playing, my cousin showed firmness and decision. Since marrying and taking charge of affairs in that mansion, she has grown all the more experienced and accomplished. I have thought it over for several days, and there is no one but my cousin whom I can ask. Even if you will not do it for my sake or my wife’s, Aunt, please do it for the sake of the one who has died!” As he spoke, tears rolled down his cheeks.

p.src: What worried Lady Wang was that Xifeng had never managed a funeral and might make a poor job of it and expose herself to ridicule. But seeing Jia Zhen plead so desperately, she began to waver, though she merely gazed thoughtfully at Xifeng. Xifeng had always loved taking charge of affairs and showing off her abilities. Although she managed her own household competently, she had never overseen a wedding or funeral and feared that people still did not fully respect her; she had longed for just such an opportunity. Now that Jia Zhen had made this request, she was already delighted inwardly. At first she had seen Lady Wang refuse, but then Jia Zhen spoke with such sincerity that Lady Wang seemed inclined to relent. Xifeng therefore said to her, “Elder Brother has asked so earnestly, Madam; please agree.” Lady Wang asked softly, “Are you capable of it?” “Why should I not be?” replied Xifeng. Elder Brother has already put all the important matters outside in order. I need only supervise the inner household, and if there is anything I do not know, I can simply ask you, Madam.” Lady Wang saw the sense in this and said no more. Seeing that Xifeng had agreed, Jia Zhen again smiled ingratiatingly and said, “There is no help for it now; whatever happens, I must ask my dear cousin to undertake this burden. Let me first bow to you here, Cousin; when everything is over, I shall visit your mansion and offer my thanks again.” With that, he bowed deeply, and Xifeng hastened to return his courtesy.

p.src: Jia Zhen hurriedly drew the Ningguo Mansion’s paired tally from his sleeve and told Baoyu to give it to Xifeng. He added, “Do whatever you think best. Whatever you need, use this to obtain it; there is no need to ask me. Only do not deliberately try to save me money: appearances must come first. And you must treat the servants as you do in your own mansion; do not hold back merely for fear that people may complain. Apart from those two points, I have no other concerns.” Xifeng did not dare accept the tally at once but merely looked at Lady Wang. Lady Wang said, “Since your elder brother puts it that way, you may look after things for him. Only do not make decisions entirely on your own. If anything arises, send someone to consult your elder brother and sister-in-law; that is important.” Baoyu had already taken the tally from Jia Zhen’s hand and pressed it upon Xifeng. Jia Zhen then asked, “Will you stay here, Cousin, or come every day? Coming every day would make the burden still heavier. It would be better if I had a courtyard prepared at once, so that you could stay here in peace for the next few days.” “There is no need,” Xifeng said with a smile. They cannot do without me over there either, so it will be better for me to come every day.” Hearing this, Jia Zhen had no choice but to abandon the idea. After chatting idly for a while longer, he finally went out.

p.src: Xifeng went to sit in a three-bay side hall and reflected: First, the household was crowded and disorderly, so things were lost. Second, no one had clearly assigned duties, so when deadlines came, responsibility was shifted from one person to another. Third, expenses were excessive, with indiscriminate disbursements and fraudulent claims. Fourth, tasks great and small were distributed unfairly, leaving some with hard work and others with easy duties. Fifth, the servants were arrogant and unruly: those with influence refused discipline, while those without influence had no chance to advance. These five abuses were indeed customary in the Ningguo Mansion. How Xifeng dealt with them will be revealed in the next chapter. The verse says:
